purpose: Compare small Pong return-law changes; this is a rule study, not a claim to have solved any candidate.
unchanged: exact loop shortcut only for deterministic stateless policies
evaluation: All five serves, both side assignments, identical seeds across rules and policies. 640 rallies per matchup; paired seed is statistical resampling unit. Freeze policies and models before final run; no training against final seeds.
comparisons: adaptive attack vs delayed defense sensitivity proxy
retrained plain MLP vs adapted scripts and starting Contender
decision_criteria: Adaptive attackers can score against rule-aware defense from standard serves; empty safe bands alone are insufficient.
Scored rallies persist beyond immediate serve returns without large first-receiver bias.
Learned models improve with matched training opportunity; weak transfer alone is not evidence of good rules.
Preserve minimum 26-tick cross-court reaction window; delayed scripts are sensitivity checks, not human playtests.
Prefer angle-only if similarly effective because it adds no new mechanic.
Do not promote a new arena rules version on this experiment alone if adaptive defense still dominates or keyboard playability is unverified.
limitations: Finite opponents do not establish optimal play.
Limited weight search is a training probe, not a learning ceiling.
No actual human playtest has yet been performed.
